summary: Indie pop/rock: 100-140 BPM, a roomy acoustic kit played simply, a picked bass on steady root 8ths, jangly clean guitar chords (I-iii-vi-IV), a glockenspiel or guitar hook, a little raw; knowledge/style/indie.json is its template
body: Tempo 100-140 BPM, often 110-130; indie pop a bit faster and brighter than indie rock.
Drums: a live acoustic kit, simple and consistent: kick 1 and 3, snare 2 and 4, straight 8th hats; punchy, a little dirty and roomy, energetic tom and cymbal fills; restrained reverb.
Bass: a picked electric bass on simple steady root 8ths, locked to the kick, anchoring the pocket.
Harmony: plain triads, I-V-vi-IV and the indie colours I-iii-vi-IV, I-ii-IV-vi; strummed or arpeggiated clean (jangly) or crunchy guitars in the mids.
Lead: the vocal; instrumental hooks on a glockenspiel, a clean guitar line or a simple synth.
Texture/master: natural and a bit raw, mid-forward, light compression, each instrument separated; never hyper-polished.

Sources (2026-11-26): UJAM 'The Ultimate Guide to Indie Rock'; Mixdown '10 essential indie rock music production techniques'; Splice 'How to make indie pop music: a production walkthrough with Lyncs'; iZotope '3 tips for mastering indie rock'.

Apply: pattern/gmd-rock-indie-beat-1 on the drums, then pattern/prog-indie-characteristic-3 on the keys four bars later. For a whole style change the Team Lead's restyle uses knowledge/style/indie.json instead.

drums.about: the drum track (a kit); leave out if there isn't one

keys.about: a chordal part (keys, pad); leave out if there isn't one

key.about: the project's key; leave out to estimate it from the notes
